data.source_title: Suspected scaphoid injuries managed by MRI direct from the emergency department: a single-centre prospective cohort study
data.locator: Results; MRI findings among patients who completed MRI (n=208).
data.source_setting: Single-centre UK emergency department MRI pathway; patients aged 12+ with suspected scaphoid fracture and normal scaphoid-series radiographs after clinical assessment.
data.source_period: Prospective cohort enrollment: end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcome follow-up, EHR searched January 2021; article published 2021.
data.source_n: 208 completed MRI scans; 258 referred from 337 assessed.
data.quantity: MRI-detected occult scaphoid fracture among completed scans
data.unit: patients; source-reported percent and separately calculated percent
data.source_evidence_basis: Prospective service evaluation reports 27 scaphoid fractures among 208 completed scans (reported 13%).
data.limitations: Selected patients referred based on examination and radiograph review; single centre; ages 12+ (not adult-only); MRI completion denominator differs from 258 referred. This is not an unconditional probability for all wrist injuries or all negative radiographs.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Calibration comparator only for a clinician-selected suspected-scaphoid subgroup sent for MRI; do not transfer to all negative wrist films or treat as an RWJ estimate.

data.source_title: Suspected scaphoid injuries managed by MRI direct from the emergency department: a single-centre prospective cohort study
data.locator: Results; MRI findings among 208 completed scans.
data.source_setting: Single-centre UK emergency department MRI pathway; selected suspected scaphoid injuries with negative radiographs.
data.source_period: Prospective cohort enrollment: end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcome follow-up, EHR searched January 2021; article published 2021.
data.quantity: Alternative or no abnormality MRI findings
data.source_evidence_basis: Full-text Results gives six MRI outcome categories among 208: scaphoid fracture 27, other fracture 45, scaphoid contusion 13, other contusion/ligament injury 42, degenerative only 21, normal 60. Counts sum to 208; the 27 scaphoid fractures were omitted from the earlier value list.
data.limitations: Mutually exclusive MRI outcome categories reported in the Results sum to 208; separate Table III describes concurrent associated injuries, so these category counts should not be conflated with that table. Selected pathway referrals, patients aged 12+, and single-centre setting limit transfer.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as a distributional external comparator for MRI-result branches after clinician-selected imaging; retain separate occult fracture, other injury, and normal outcomes.

data.source_title: Suspected scaphoid injuries managed by MRI direct from the emergency department: a single-centre prospective cohort study
data.locator: Results; ED discharge and re-presentation after MRI.
data.source_setting: Single-centre UK emergency department MRI pathway; selected patients with suspected scaphoid injury.
data.source_period: Prospective enrollment end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcomes; EHR searched January 2021.
data.source_n: 100 of 208 completed-MRI patients discharged by ED with advice; at least one year outcome follow-up and EHR search in January 2021.
data.unit: patients; reported count, not a time-standardized probability
data.source_evidence_basis: Full-text Methods state outcomes/complications were recorded at minimum one year and electronic patient records searched January 2021; Results report 100 MRI patients discharged by ED with advice and one re-presentation.
data.limitations: Single-centre selected cohort; return ascertainment used hospital electronic records, and exact index date for the 100 discharges is not specified. Re-presentation is not equivalent to missed fracture or failed follow-up.
data.inferred_scenario_use: May inform a qualitative return branch only; do not encode as a calibrated unplanned-return probability without defined follow-up horizon and comparable ascertainment.

data.source_period: Prospective cohort enrollment: end September 2018 through end September 2019; minimum one-year outcome follow-up, EHR searched January 2021; article published 2021.
data.source_n: 258 referred for MRI; 208 completed, 45 did not attend, 5 did not tolerate the scan
data.quantity: MRI completion and reasons for noncompletion among referred patients
data.source_evidence_basis: Original cohort reports 208 completed scans among 258 referrals, with 45 nonattendances and five patients unable to tolerate MRI.
data.limitations: Single selected UK referral pathway, ages 12 and older. MRI nonattendance is not failure of all subsequent follow-up or an RWJ scheduling probability. No common referral-to-scan censoring window is established here.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Separate completed, not attended and not tolerated imaging branches for scenario authoring; do not silently omit the 50 noncompleters when interpreting MRI yield.
